name: Rimewrack
specific_features: Starship crash site (poacher vessel downed by automated battery fire)
description: Rimewrack wears a shell of blue glacial ice forty kilometers thick, fractured into plates that grind and calve along fault lines visible from orbit. Auroras pool unnaturally around wandering magnetic poles, staining the horizon green over black pressure ridges. The only warmth lies far below, where geothermal vents feed a lightless ocean crusted with mineral towers taller than any terrestrial structure.

On the surface there is only wind, ice-creak, and a silence so complete that visitors report hearing their own pulse. Beneath the shell, the subglacial sea is warm and crowded: pale filter-feeding leviathans drift between the vents, singing in infrasound that makes the ice above tremble like a drum skin. Standing on the shell during a song-swarm feels less like standing on rock and more like lying on the chest of something breathing.

The leviathans' existence was confirmed eleven years ago by a survey buoy, and the confirmation leaked within a week. Vent-fields also grow dark crystals prized for focusing arrays, and harvesting them means drilling through the nursery grounds. A protectorate guild deployed automated defense platforms to enforce a moratorium; the platforms still fire on unauthorized tonnage, as the wreck of the poacher Kellion's Wake on the southern shelf demonstrates, but the guild's patrol commitments have quietly lapsed.

Every season the drill-ships come bolder and lower, probing for gaps in the coverage, and salvagers circle the Kellion's Wake like carrion birds. Biologists warn the species may be a single interconnected organism-colony, meaning one bad harvest could end a lineage older than most star nations. Somewhere below the ice, the songs have already changed key, and no one can say yet whether that is mourning or warning.
